newsitem.title: CHINA: China share indices end up on improved sentiment.
newsitem.headline: China share indices end up on improved sentiment.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended up sharply on Friday due to bargain-hunting with sentiment improving after recent falls, brokers said.
Bargain-hunting after recent falls helped propel the markets higher, as well as buying of companies expected to post strong interim results, they said.
Shanghai's foreign currency B share index rose 1.020 points or 1.36 percent to 75.861 on volume of 10.513 million shares worth $6.376 million.
The Shenzhen B index leapt 6.77 points or 5.39 percent to 132.36 on turnover of HK$87.8 million.
Meanwhile, Shanghai's domestic currency A share index rose 36.733 points or 3.14 percent to 1,206.722 points on volume of 376.044 million shares worth 4.558 billion yuan.
Shanghai's SSE30 blue chip index rose 101.394 points or 2.75 percent to to 3,793.472 points.
The Shenzhen A index roared up 17.88 points or 4.70 percent to 398.22 on turnover of 5.6 billion yuan, compared with Thursday's 4.4 billion.
"The (Shanghai) B shares gained because previous falls were overdone," said a broker at Shenzhen J&A Securities in Shanghai. "But the expectations of investors are still not that good."
An analyst at China Southern Securities said: "Both the (Shenzhen) A and B share markets are staging strong technical rebounds after the recent plunges gave them no room to fall any further.
"Many investors picked relatively cheap shares in companies expected to post strong interim results, and that pushed up the indices," the analyst said.
Shenzhen-listed firms must publish their 1997 first-half results by August 30.
Shanghai Sanmao Textiles Co was the top Shanghai B share gainer on bargain hunting, rising $0.012 or 9.09 percent to $0.144.

Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development Co was the most heavily traded Shanghai B share. The stock was hit by profit-taking, falling $0.012 or 0.94 percent to $1.268 on volume of 850,080 shares.
Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd, a market heavyweight, was among the heaviest Shenzhen B share gainers and surged to its 10 percent limit-up at HK$2.93.
Recently listed Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd was the most heavily traded Shenzhen counter on volume of 3.6 million shares, rising HK$0.54 to HK$7.45.
The impact of the suspension of Shenzen-listed Foshan Lighting and Electrical Co Ltd on Friday for illegal loans was downplayed by the markets in both Shenzhen and Shanghai, brokers said.
"Foshan's punishment is a small part of the government's securities clean-up drive, which everyone has got used to," said one analyst.
Foshan said in a statement on Friday it was fined one million yuan and had its illegal profits confiscated.
